name: outline_sections
line: Split a LaTeX file of the workspace into its sections: each title with its body text.

sections.title: Setup
sections.text: Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be compact and $f\colon K \to \mathbb{R}$ continuous.

sections.title: Main bound
sections.text: We claim $\sup_K |f| \le 1$. The proof is omitted.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: The bound is sharp for constant functions.

round1.reason: The Setup section only fixes hypotheses and asserts nothing that needs proof, so it is internally sound as written; however these assumptions are far too weak for what the paper builds on them — a continuous function on a compact set need not satisfy $\sup_K|f|\le 1$ — so the gap lies downstream in "Main bound", not here.

round2.claim: We claim $\sup_K |f| \le 1$. The proof is omitted.
round2.reason: Nothing in the draft bounds $f$: from "K compact, f continuous" alone any continuous f is allowed, and f ≡ 2 on nonempty K gives $\sup_K|f| = 2 > 1$, so the claim is false as written rather than merely unproved. Omitting the proof removes the only place a missing hypothesis (e.g. $\|f\|_\infty \le 1$ or a normalization) could have been supplied.
